question: Who initiated the Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)** was launched by the **Central Government** of India in **September 2001**.
 
• The program aimed to provide **employment opportunities** in rural areas and ensure food security by offering wages partly in cash and partly in food grains.
 
• It was designed to improve the **economic conditions of rural households** and reduce unemployment in rural India.* Hence, the Central Government initiated this program.*
 
• The scheme was a consolidation of two earlier schemes: the **Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS)** and the **Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana (JGSY)**, reflecting a more comprehensive approach to rural employment generation.
 
• It was implemented through the **Panchayati Raj Institutions**, ensuring decentralized governance and participation of local self-governments.* However, the initiation was done by the Central Government.*
 
• The scheme addressed rural infrastructure development by funding labor-intensive projects such as the construction of roads, irrigation facilities, and rural housing.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Central Government.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY):**

 
 
• The scheme was targeted at rural areas, focusing on providing **employment opportunities** to the poor and ensuring their basic needs through wage employment.
 
• Under the program, wages were paid in a combination of **cash and food grains**, ensuring both income generation and food security.
 
• The scheme was financed by the **Central Government** and supplemented by the **State Governments**. However, the **major funding** and overall management were under the purview of the Central Government.
 
 
 
• **Implementation of the Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme was implemented through **Panchayati Raj Institutions**, enabling decentralized and participatory governance for rural development.
 
• The funds allocated under the scheme were used for labor-intensive projects such as the construction of rural roads, irrigation systems, and houses for the poor.
 
• It aimed to create durable assets in rural areas while addressing unemployment and underemployment among rural households.
 
 
 
• **Wider Objectives:**
 
 
• The scheme contributed to rural development by enhancing **infrastructure** and providing sustainable livelihoods to rural populations.
 
• It was a step toward eradicating poverty by ensuring employment and improving the standard of living in rural areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics:**

 
 
• The SGRY scheme ensured **equal participation** of women, aiming to empower them economically and socially.
 
• The allocation of food grains under the scheme was significant, addressing the issue of **malnutrition** and hunger in rural India.
 
 
 
• **Notable Achievements:**
 
 
• The scheme improved rural **employment rates** and contributed to the creation of durable assets in many regions.
 
• It enhanced the quality of life in rural areas by addressing both economic and food-related challenges.
